title: What to expect when you write to me
subtitle: How the arrangement works, from your first note to the flight home.

text: There's no form to fill in. You just write.
sub: The first exchange is a conversation about where you're leaning, and vague is fine. Most good trips start that way.

items.head: You write
items.body: A region, a month, an anniversary you want to do properly. That's plenty.

items.head: I edit
items.body: Any search engine can find a hundred sailings. I'll send you the three I'd actually book, and why.

items.head: We settle it
items.body: Ship, cabin, dining time, the fare. You make the calls and I do the paperwork.

items.head: I stay on it
items.body: I keep watching the fare after you book, and if something goes sideways mid-trip you call me.

text: If a celebrated itinerary is wrong for you, I'll say so.
sub: Talking someone out of the wrong ship is half the job. The fare conversation only starts once the ship is right.

quote: The line pays me after you sail. Your fare is the same or better, and my services are complimentary.

title: Send this to the person you'd sail with
body: Most trips start as a conversation between two people. When yours does, you know where I am.
